title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a group-theoretic lemma. The lemma says the functor (Ens_4, bijections) → (groups isomorphic to S_4, isomorphisms), I ↦ S_I, is an equivalence. Equivalently, S_4 has trivial centre and only inner automorphisms. To prove it, Grothendieck builds a quasi-inverse G ↦ I_G, where I_G is the set of 3-Sylow subgroups of G (there are 4). He also recovers the affine-plane structure on I, i.e. a torsor structure under a 2-dimensional F_2-vector space V.

Steps:
(1) Let V be the maximal abelian normal subgroup of G (the Klein four-group). V is a 2-dimensional F_2-vector space and G/V ≅ Aut_{F_2}(V) = GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_J. Here J is the 3-element set of nonzero elements of V*, i.e. the directions or lines of the affine plane.
(2) S_J has a unique 3-Sylow subgroup, S_J^+ = [S_J,S_J] (≅A_3), of index 2. Let G^+ be its preimage (≅A_4). The 3-Sylows of G are exactly the complements ('scindages') of V in 1→V→G^+→S_J^+→1.
(3) V acts on these complements by conjugation. The action is transitive: by coprimality (Schur–Zassenhaus), H^1(C_3,V)=0. It is free because V^{S_J^+}=0, since a 3-cycle permutes the three nonzero elements of V* circularly. So I_G is a V-torsor, i.e. an affine plane over F_2.
(4) For G=S_I there is a natural bijection I → I_{S_I}, i ↦ A_{I∖{i}}, the unique 3-Sylow fixing i. This gives a natural isomorphism from the identity functor to the composite I ↦ I_{S_I}.

The next page gives the other composite: G acts on I_G by conjugation, giving G ≅ S_{I_G}. It then classifies the elements of S_4 by their affine and cube-rotation meaning.

Purpose in the manuscript on elliptic moduli in characteristic ≠2: the 4 branch points of E → P^1 (or the 4 points of a 2-division torsor) form a 4-element set that is canonically an affine plane under E[2]. The group S_4 → S_3 = GL(E[2]) governs passing from 4 marked points on P^1 to level-2 structures (the λ/j picture). This page is preparatory, intrinsic group theory.
errors: Notational slip: Grothendieck writes J = V*, but S_J ≅ S_3 requires J to be the 3-element set of nonzero elements of V* (equivalently the lines of V), not all of V*.

Transitivity of V on the set of complements is asserted without comment. It relies on H^1(S_J^+,V)=0, which follows from coprime orders (Schur–Zassenhaus). The invariant statement V^{S_J^+}=0 that he cites gives freeness (and, combined with |V| = number of complements = 4, transitivity by counting). This is a minor gap only.

ideas.what: S_4 is a complete group: the functor I ↦ S_I from 4-element sets to groups isomorphic to S_4 is fully faithful, with explicit quasi-inverse G ↦ {3-Sylow subgroups of G}.
ideas.modern_name: Completeness of S_n (n≠2,6); groupoid equivalence BS_4 ≃ groupoid of S_4-type groups

ideas.what: The set of 3-Sylows of S_4 is a torsor under the Klein four-group V, identified with the set of complements of V in A_4. This is the canonical affine-plane-over-F_2 structure on a 4-element set.
ideas.modern_name: Complements as a torsor under Z^1=B^1 (Schur–Zassenhaus with H^1=0); Ens_4 ≃ affine planes over F_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schur–Zassenhaus, standard cohomology of group extensions)

ideas.what: Recovering the 4-element set intrinsically via i ↦ A_{I∖{i}} (the 3-Sylow fixing i), giving a natural isomorphism from the identity functor.
ideas.modern_name: Natural reconstruction of a G-set from its stabilizers

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, functorial (choice-free) restatement of classical facts about S_4: completeness, the Klein normal subgroup, and the Sylows as a V-torsor. It serves as a preparatory lemma for level-2 structures on elliptic curves. It is elegant in Grothendieck's canonical-identification style, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'torseur sous Ext Ver' is likely 'torseur sous V' (the torsor structure under V). The rest of the line is uncertain.
'les I_G est bien un torseur sous V' should read 'donc I_G est bien un torseur sous V'.
The extension should read 1 → V → G^+ → S_J^+ → 1, with G^+ the preimage of S_J^+ (≅ A_4).

Last lines: likely 'Ainsi les foncteurs I ↦ S_I, G ↦ I_G, et la composition I → I(S_I), on a un isomorphisme de l'identité [avec le] foncteur composé'. This is the natural isomorphism id ≅ composite; the reading is uncertain.
